proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(E_0\) for \(E_{P_{0,O}}\), put \(G_b=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}\), and stack the profiled restriction maps over the finitely many strata. All expectations below are under \(P_{0,O}\).

We first profile the PT restriction. By \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\),
\[
 q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x),
 \qquad
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}=I_J-J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Direct multiplication gives
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}\mathbf 1_J
 =\mathbf 1_J-J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}\mathbf 1_J)
 =0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Therefore, along every regular path, including a path with arbitrary derivative \(\dot\delta_1^0(x)\),
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot q_{\mathrm{PT},x}
 =A_{\mathrm{PT}}\{\dot\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-\dot D(x)\}
 =-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot D(x).
 \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3), \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) show that the observed profiled restriction is \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\) and its Riesz representer is \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}\). The matrix \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) is symmetric and idempotent, its null space is \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_J\}\), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm{PT}})=J-1.
 \tag{4}
\]
If \(\widetilde R_{D,x}\) represents the derivative of \(D(x)\), then (3) gives \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\widetilde R_{D,x}\). Thus
\[
 \operatorname{rank}E_0[R_{\mathrm{PT},x}R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}]
 \le \operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm{PT}})=J-1.
 \tag{5}
\]
Under the nondegeneracy condition in the statement, the left side of (5) is \(J-1\).

The analogous SC calculation supplies the requested additional rank information without a new assumption. Put
\[
 \Pi_x=B(x)\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}sc\text{-}rank}\) makes \(B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\) invertible. Hence \(\Pi_x\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{col}B(x)\), with
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(I_T-\Pi_x)=T-J.
 \tag{7}
\]
At an SC law, \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\). Differentiating \(\Pi_xB(x)=B(x)\) along an arbitrary regular path gives
\[
 \dot\Pi_x B(x)+\Pi_x\dot B(x)=\dot B(x),
 \qquad
 \dot\Pi_x B(x)w(x)=(I_T-\Pi_x)\dot B(x)w(x).
 \tag{8}
\]
Since \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=(I_T-\Pi_x)a(x)\), equations (8) and \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\) yield
\[
 \dot r_{\mathrm{SC},x}
 =(I_T-\Pi_x)\{\dot a(x)-\dot B(x)w(x)\}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus, if \(\widetilde R_{C,x}\) is any vector of Riesz representers for the coordinates of \(\dot a(x)-\dot B(x)w(x)\), then
\[
 R_{\mathrm{SC},x}=(I_T-\Pi_x)\widetilde R_{C,x}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{rank}E_0[R_{\mathrm{SC},x}R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}]
 \le T-J.
 \tag{11}
\]
Equality holds exactly when the covariance form of the residualized coordinates in (10) is positive definite on \(\operatorname{range}(I_T-\Pi_x)\); this is the stated corresponding nondegeneracy condition. Notice that (11) is a rank conclusion, not an added rank premise.

We next identify the observed projections of the causal branches. For PT, \(r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=0\) is equivalent to \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)=0\), and (4) makes this equivalent to
\[
 D(x)=c(x)\mathbf 1_J
 \quad\text{for some scalar }c(x).
 \tag{12}
\]
Every compatible PT law satisfies (12): no anticipation makes donor final changes observable, and conditional parallel trends equates each of them to \(\delta_1^0(x)\). Conversely, if an observed law satisfies (12), retain every observed coordinate and choose the unobserved treated-group variable \(Y_T(0)\), conditionally on \(X=x\), to have mean \(\mu_{1,T-1}(x)+c(x)\); before period \(T\), impose no anticipation. This constructs a compatible full-data PT extension without changing the observed law. Thus the observed projection of the PT branch is locally the zero set of its profiled restriction.

For SC, the rank assumption makes \(w(x)\) unique, and
\[
 r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (I_T-\Pi_x)a(x)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a(x)=B(x)w(x).
 \tag{13}
\]
The first row of (13) is \(1=\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}w(x)\). Under no anticipation, the remaining rows are the preperiod restrictions in \(\mathrm{ass{:}synthetic\text{-}mean}\). Conversely, from an observed law satisfying (13), retain the observed coordinates and choose the missing treated-group \(Y_T(0)\), conditionally on \(X=x\), to have mean
\[
 \sum_{g=2}^{J+1}w_g(x)\mu_{g,T}(x).
 \tag{14}
\]
Equations (13)--(14) construct a compatible full-data SC extension satisfying the final-period restriction. The rank margin makes \(w(x)\) a smooth function of the observed conditional means. Hence the observed projection of the SC branch is locally the zero set of its profiled restriction.

We now prove the tangent-space equality. If \(s\) is the score of a branch-preserving quadratic-mean differentiable submodel, differentiating \(r_{b,x}=0\) and applying \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\) yields
\[
 E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.
 \tag{15}
\]
This proves one inclusion. For the converse, use \(\mathrm{ass{:}normal\text{-}rank}\) and the retained-coordinate convention in the definition of \(R_b\) to choose, throughout a neighborhood of \(P_0\), a maximal independent coordinate vector \(r_b^{\ast}\) with gradient vector \(R_b^{\ast}\). The other displayed coordinates impose no additional local equation. Linear independence in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\) implies that there are bounded, mean-zero functions \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\) for which
\[
 M=E_0[R_b^{\ast}v^{\prime}]
 \quad\text{is nonsingular},
 \qquad v=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)^{\prime}.
 \tag{16}
\]
Indeed, the Gram matrix of \(R_b^{\ast}\) is positive definite; truncating and recentering its coordinates gives bounded functions whose cross-moment matrix converges to that Gram matrix, so a sufficiently late truncation satisfies (16).

Let \(s\) first be bounded, mean zero, and satisfy (15). Define the finite-dimensional exponential-tilt chart
\[
 \frac{dP_{O,\varepsilon,c}}{dP_{0,O}}(o)
 =\frac{\exp\{\varepsilon s(o)+c^{\prime}v(o)\}}
 {E_0[\exp\{\varepsilon s+c^{\prime}v\}]},
 \qquad
 F(\varepsilon,c)=r_b^{\ast}(P_{O,\varepsilon,c}).
 \tag{17}
\]
Boundedness in (17), finite support of \(X\) and \(G\), the positive cell margins, and the fourth-moment bound justify differentiation of every conditional mean entering \(F\). Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\), (15), and (16) give
\[
 F(0,0)=0,
 \qquad
 \partial_cF(0,0)=M,
 \qquad
 \partial_\varepsilon F(0,0)=E_0[R_b^{\ast}s]=0.
 \tag{18}
\]
Differentiability gives
\[
 F(\varepsilon,c)=F(\varepsilon,0)+Mc+\zeta(\varepsilon,c),
 \qquad
 \|\zeta(\varepsilon,c)\|=o(|\varepsilon|+\|c\|),
 \tag{19}
\]
with the derivative of \(\zeta\) in \(c\) arbitrarily small on a sufficiently small neighborhood. On a ball \(\|c\|\le C|\varepsilon|\), the map
\[
 c\longmapsto-M^{-1}\{F(\varepsilon,0)+\zeta(\varepsilon,c)\}
 \tag{20}
\]
is a contraction of that ball into itself. Its fixed point \(c(\varepsilon)\) satisfies \(F(\varepsilon,c(\varepsilon))=0\). The last equality in (18) gives \(F(\varepsilon,0)=o(\varepsilon)\), whence
\[
 c(0)=0,
 \qquad
 c(\varepsilon)=o(\varepsilon).
 \tag{21}
\]
The corrected path therefore has score \(s\). Its full profiled restriction vanishes by the locally fixed maximal coordinate system, and the extensions in (12)--(14) lift it to a full-data path in branch \(b\). The fixed interior support, moment, and rank margins at \(P_0\) ensure that a sufficiently short segment remains in the branch model.

For an arbitrary \(s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}\) satisfying (15), let \(\widetilde s_k\) be its truncation at level \(k\), recentered to have mean zero, and set
\[
 s_k=\widetilde s_k-v^{\prime}M^{-1}E_0[R_b^{\ast}\widetilde s_k].
 \tag{22}
\]
Then \(s_k\) is bounded and mean zero, (16) gives \(E_0[R_b^{\ast}s_k]=0\), and Cauchy--Schwarz together with \(\widetilde s_k\to s\) in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\) gives
\[
 E_0[R_b^{\ast}\widetilde s_k]\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \|s_k-s\|_{P_0,2}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{23}
\]
The bounded case puts every \(s_k\) in the branch tangent set, and \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\text{-}tangents}\) takes its \(L^2\)-closure. Combining (15) and (23) proves
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)
 =\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0
       \text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{24}
\]

There are finitely many retained normals, so elementary orthogonal-complement algebra applied to (24) gives
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)^{\perp}
 =\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{25}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\), \(E_0[G_bs]=\dot\theta_b(s)\) for every unrestricted score. Hence \(\mathrm{def{:}influence\text{-}classes}\) and (24)--(25) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal I_b(P_0)
 &=\{\phi\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_0[(\phi-G_b)s]=0
       \text{ for every }s\in\mathcal T_b(P_0)\}\\
 &=G_b+\mathcal T_b(P_0)^{\perp}
 =G_b+\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{26}
\]

Finally, let
\[
 \Gamma_b=E_0[R_bR_b^{\prime}],
 \qquad
 u_b=E_0[R_bG_b].
 \tag{27}
\]
If \(c\in\ker(\Gamma_b)\), then \(E_0[(c^{\prime}R_b)^2]=0\), so \(c^{\prime}R_b=0\) almost surely and \(c^{\prime}u_b=0\). Thus \(u_b\in\operatorname{range}(\Gamma_b)\). For every coefficient vector \(a\), the Moore--Penrose projection identity gives
\[
 \|G_b+R_b^{\prime}a\|_{P_0,2}^2
 =\|G_b-R_b^{\prime}\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b\|_{P_0,2}^2
 +(a+\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b)^{\prime}
   \Gamma_b(a+\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b).
 \tag{28}
\]
The second term is nonnegative. Minimizing (28) over (26) proves
\[
 \phi_b
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}
 -R_b^{\prime}\{E_0[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\}^{\dagger}
 E_0\!\left[R_b\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{b,x}\right].
 \tag{29}
\]
Because (29) is the Hilbert-space projection itself, redundant displayed rows affect coefficient coordinates but not the represented function. Equations (5) and (11) additionally record the sharp dimensional ceilings \(J-1\) and \(T-J\) for the displayed PT and SC normal Grams, with equality under the respective residualized-coordinate nondegeneracy conditions.

If \(J=1\), then \(\mathbf 1_J\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}=1\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\) gives
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}=I_1-1=0,
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=0.
 \tag{1}
\]
The tangent normal form therefore yields
\[
 \mathcal T_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)=\mathcal H_{P_0},
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
In particular, the SC tangent space is a subspace of the unrestricted PT observed tangent space.

Derivative compatibility must still be checked. With one donor, the intercept restriction forces \(w_2(x)=1\), and the SC restriction gives
\[
 \mu_{1,t}(x)=\mu_{2,t}(x),
 \qquad t<T.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus at every nearby law in the SC branch,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_O)
 &=\pi_1^{-1}\sum_xp_X(x)p_1(x)
 \{\mu_{1,T}(x)-\mu_{1,T-1}(x)-\mu_{2,T}(x)+\mu_{2,T-1}(x)\}\\
 &=\pi_1^{-1}\sum_xp_X(x)p_1(x)
 \{\mu_{1,T}(x)-\mu_{2,T}(x)\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_O),
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
where (3) at \(t=T-1\) gives the second equality. Hence the two functional derivatives agree along every SC tangent score. Since \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\) represents the derivative of \(\theta_{\mathrm{PT}}\) on all of \(\mathcal H_{P_0}\), equation (4) implies \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\). Therefore
\[
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0),
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)
 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\}.
 \tag{5}
\]
The definitions of \(\phi_U\) and \(V_U\) now give \(\phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\) and \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}\).

For \(T=2\), write \(\Delta Y=Y_2-Y_1\) and
\[
 m_g(x)=E_O[\Delta Y\mid G=g,X=x].
\]
Overlap gives \(p_1(x)>0\), \(p_2(x)>0\), and \(\pi_1>0\), so every following division is valid. Direct differentiation of the PT observed-law functional gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}(O)
 &=\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=1\}}{\pi_1}\{\Delta Y-m_1(X)\}
 -\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=2\}}{\pi_1}\frac{p_1(X)}{p_2(X)}
   \{\Delta Y-m_2(X)\}\\
 &\quad+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=1\}}{\pi_1}
 \{m_1(X)-m_2(X)-\theta\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{6}
\]
The first two terms have conditional mean zero. The last is centered because \(\theta=E_O[m_1(X)-m_2(X)\mid G=1]\), and it is the derivative contribution from the treated covariate distribution. Thus (6) is mean zero, and direct pathwise differentiation verifies its covariance equation for every unrestricted observed score. Under the relabeling of treated and comparison indicators as \(G=1\) and \(G=2\), equation (6) is the panel ATT efficient influence function in \(\mathrm{lem{:}santanna\text{-}zhao\text{-}panel\text{-}did\text{-}gradient}\).

The obstruction is caused by the quantifiers in \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}union\text{-}sequences}\), not by infeasibility of the center QP. Choose the fixed margins so that \(P^{\star}\) satisfies the overlap, fourth-moment, rank, spectral-gap, and variance conditions with strict slack. For a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta\ne0\), retain the donor means and every innovation law of \(P^{\star}\), but replace the treated untreated mean path by
\[
 (1/2+\delta)(-1,-2,-2)+(1/2-\delta)(1,2,2)
 =(-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta).
 \tag{1}
\]
Give the treated group the same additive final-period treatment effect as under \(P^{\star}\), and call the resulting law \(Q_\delta\). The treated and both donor untreated final changes remain zero, so conditional parallel trends holds. The donor matrix is unchanged, and (1) is reproduced by the unique weights
\[
 w_\delta=(1/2+\delta,1/2-\delta)^{\prime}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus the synthetic-mean restriction also holds. Group and stratum probabilities are unchanged, while all innovations remain bounded. The structurally zero Gram directions persist, and the nonzero eigenvalues and local-score variance are continuous in \(\delta\). The strict margins therefore persist for all sufficiently small \(|\delta|\). Hence \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and satisfies every coordinatewise margin in the local-sequence definition.

Fix an integer \(m\). Construct two triangular sequences. In each sequence set the law at coordinate \(m\) equal to \(Q_\delta\) and every other coordinate equal to \(P^{\star}\). Label coordinate \(m\) by PT in the first sequence and by SC in the second, using any admissible label elsewhere. Each sequence belongs to \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\): after its single exceptional coordinate it is identically \(P^{\star}\), so its QMD expansion holds eventually with score zero and remainder zero, and both possible coordinate laws obey the fixed margins. Thus, for every sample size \(m\), the supremum over the frozen sequence class contains two labeled copies of the same observed law \(Q_\delta\) at that coordinate.

For the no-covariate equal-share witness define the centered cell-mean score
\[
 z_{g,t}(O)=3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\{Y_t-\mu_{g,t}\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Then \(E_{Q_\delta}[z_{g,t}]=0\) and, by the displayed innovation variances,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{2,3})=3\sigma_{2,3}^2=\frac32,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{3,3})=3\sigma_{3,3}^2=6.
 \tag{4}
\]
At \(P^{\star}\), \(\mathrm{prop{:}strict\text{-}three\text{-}group\text{-}witness}\) shows that the common score has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\). The PT chart extension freezes its normal coefficient at \(P^{\star}\), and the donor laws are unchanged, so its final donor coefficients at \(Q_\delta\) remain \((-1/2,-1/2)\). By contrast, the SC normal depends only on preperiod coordinates, while (2) makes the final donor coefficients of the unrestricted SC gradient \((-1/2-\delta,-1/2+\delta)\). Therefore, for
\[
 \Delta_\delta
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})
  -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star}),
 \tag{5}
\]
the final-innovation component is \(\delta(z_{2,3}-z_{3,3})\). Every remaining component uses other group-period innovations. Disjoint group indicators and independence across periods make those components orthogonal to the displayed component. Equations (3)--(4) therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 &\ge\delta^2\{\operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{2,3})
                 +\operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{3,3})\}\\
 &=\delta^2\left(\frac32+6\right)
 =\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{6}
\]
Both chart extensions in \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}score\text{-}extension}\) are sums of mean-zero gradient and normal representers, so \(E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta]=0\).

Suppose one estimator satisfied the requested asymptotic-linear expansion uniformly over \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\) and every admissible chart label. At sample size \(m\), apply it to the two sequences just constructed and couple them through the identical iid sample from \(Q_\delta\). The estimator and the causal target on the left side are identical under the two labels. Subtracting the two expansions and their uniformly negligible remainders would imply
\[
 S_m:=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta_\delta(O_i)=o_{Q_\delta}(1).
 \tag{7}
\]
By iid sampling and centering,
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2]=E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 \ge\frac{15}{2}\delta^2.
 \tag{8}
\]
Moreover, \(\Delta_\delta\) is a bounded linear combination of finitely many Rademacher innovations. Expanding the fourth power of a sum of independent centered variables and retaining the terms whose indices occur in pairs gives
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^4]
 =m^{-1}E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^4]
  +3(1-m^{-1})E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]^2,
 \tag{9}
\]
which is bounded uniformly in \(m\). In fact, if the bound in (9) is \(C\), then for every \(A>0\),
\[
 \sup_m E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2\mathbf 1\{S_m^2>A\}]
 \le \frac{C}{A}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Thus \((S_m^2)_m\) is uniformly integrable. If (7) held, then for every fixed \(A\) and \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2\mathbf 1\{S_m^2\le A\}]
 \le \varepsilon+A\,Q_\delta(S_m^2>\varepsilon)\longrightarrow\varepsilon.
 \tag{11}
\]
First choose \(A\) so that the right side of (10) is arbitrarily small, then send \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) in (11). This proves \(E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2]\to0\), contradicting (8).

No estimator can therefore possess both chart expansions uniformly over the frozen sequence class. Since asymptotic linearity is a required conjunct of the requested four-part construction, the entire affirmative result, including variance consistency and multiplier coverage, is false under the frozen definition. The branch-chart extensions used here are definitions that formulate the contradiction; this proof establishes no positive sequencewise continuation theorem. It merely leaves open whether one can prove such a result after replacing the frozen class by a genuinely uniform neighborhood with common score and remainder bounds and no arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.

Write \(E_0\) for expectation under \(P_{0,O}\), put \(u=J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J\), and let \(\mu_{C,t}(x)=(\mu_{2,t}(x),\ldots,\mu_{J+1,t}(x))^{\prime}\). We first prove identification rather than assigning a causal meaning by definition. No anticipation gives \(Y_t=Y_t(0)\) for \(t<T\), and every donor is untreated at \(T\). Under conditional parallel trends,
\[
 \delta_1^0(x)=\Delta\mu_g(x),
 \qquad g=2,\ldots,J+1.
 \tag{1}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_F[Y_T(1)-Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]
 &=\mu_{1,T}(x)-\mu_{1,T-1}(x)-\delta_1^0(x)\\
 &=\mu_{1,T}(x)-\mu_{1,T-1}(x)-u^{\prime}D(x).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
The cell-mass and overlap assumptions give
\[
 \pi_1=\sum_xp_X(x)p_1(x)\ge K\kappa_0\epsilon_0>0,
 \tag{3}
\]
so the treated-stratum weights
\[
 \nu_x=\frac{p_X(x)p_1(x)}{\pi_1}
 \tag{4}
\]
are well defined. Averaging (2) with (4) proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_O)\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PT}}\).

Under the synthetic-mean restriction, the preperiod equations and the intercept equation give \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\), including \(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}w(x)=1\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}sc\text{-}rank}\) gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B(x)^{\prime}B(x))\ge\kappa_0>0\), so the displayed least-squares formula uniquely identifies \(w(x)\). Its final-period equation gives
\[
 E_F[Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]=w(x)^{\prime}\mu_{C,T}(x).
 \tag{5}
\]
Subtracting (5) from the observed treated final mean and averaging with (4) proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_O)\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SC}}\). Thus the two observed-law functionals agree at every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) because both equal the causal ATT there.

We next prove that the two influence-function faces meet. For one stratum define
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)=g_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a,
 \qquad
 \psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=g_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d.
 \tag{6}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\), sums of the first family exhaust \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\), and sums of the second exhaust \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\).

Suppress \(x\) and the common factor \(\nu_x\), and write a dot for a pathwise differential at \(P_0\). Because
\[
 \operatorname{range}(A_{\mathrm{PT}})
 =\{v\in\mathbb R^J:\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}v=0\},
\]
adding a PT normal permits every donor weight \(v\) satisfying \(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}v=1\). The resulting conditional-mean differential is
\[
 L_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)
 =\dot\mu_{1,T}-\dot\mu_{1,T-1}
  -v^{\prime}(\dot\mu_{C,T}-\dot\mu_{C,T-1}).
 \tag{7}
\]
At an exact SC restriction, differentiating the full-rank least-squares equation gives
\[
 \dot w=(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w).
 \tag{8}
\]
Thus the unrestricted SC differential is
\[
 \dot\mu_{1,T}-w^{\prime}\dot\mu_{C,T}
 +q_0^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w),
 \qquad
 q_0=-B(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}\mu_{C,T},
 \tag{9}
\]
where \(B^{\prime}q_0=-\mu_{C,T}\). The SC restriction normals add exactly vectors in \(\ker(B^{\prime})\), so the SC affine face consists of
\[
 L_{\mathrm{SC}}(q)
 =\dot\mu_{1,T}-w^{\prime}\dot\mu_{C,T}
  +q^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w),
 \qquad
 B^{\prime}q=-\mu_{C,T}.
 \tag{10}
\]
Let \(e_0\in\mathbb R^T\) select the intercept row and \(e_-\in\mathbb R^T\) select period \(T-1\). At the intersection, (1) supplies a scalar \(\delta_x\) such that
\[
 \mu_{C,T}=\mu_{C,T-1}+\delta_x\mathbf 1_J.
 \tag{11}
\]
Because \(B^{\prime}e_0=\mathbf 1_J\) and \(B^{\prime}e_-=\mu_{C,T-1}\),
\[
 q_*=-e_- -\delta_xe_0
 \tag{12}
\]
satisfies the constraint in (10). The intercept rows of \(a\) and \(B\) are fixed, so \(e_0^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w)=0\). Substitution into (10), followed by the preperiod matching equation, yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L_{\mathrm{SC}}(q_*)
 &=\dot\mu_{1,T}-w^{\prime}\dot\mu_{C,T}
   -\dot\mu_{1,T-1}+w^{\prime}\dot\mu_{C,T-1}\\
 &=L_{\mathrm{PT}}(w).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{13}
\]
The product-rule terms from differentiating \(\nu_x\) also coincide because the two conditional contrasts have the same value at the intersection. Restoring these terms and the factor \(\nu_x\), (13) produces a representer of both forms in (6). Therefore
\[
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\ne\varnothing.
 \tag{14}
\]

For any \((a,d)\), \(\mathrm{def{:}union\text{-}qp}\) and the definition of \(h_x\) give
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=c(a,d)^{\prime}h_x.
 \tag{15}
\]
Since \(\Omega_x\) is positive semidefinite,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Omega_x^{1/2}c(a,d)=0
 &\Longleftrightarrow c(a,d)^{\prime}\Omega_xc(a,d)=0\\
 &\Longleftrightarrow
 E_0[\{\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)\}^2\mid X=x]=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus the QP constraint is exactly equality of the two stratum representations in \(L^2(P_{0,O}\mid X=x)\), and its objective is
\[
 E_0[\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)^2\mid X=x]
 =\ell_{\mathrm{PT}}(a)^{\prime}\Omega_x\ell_{\mathrm{PT}}(a).
 \tag{17}
\]
Feasibility follows from (13). The feasible set is closed and affine, and its image in the finite-dimensional span of \(h_x\) is a closed affine subspace. Orthogonal projection of zero onto that subspace gives a unique minimizing represented function. Redundant coordinates may yield several coefficient pairs, but the Euclidean minimum-norm tie rule defines \((a_x^U,d_x^U)\). The constant-rank and positive-spectrum assumptions ensure that the retained coordinate system is stable and that no zero eigenvalue is inverted.

Functions supported on distinct strata are orthogonal, and \(p_X(x)>0\). Hence the unconditional projection separates across strata:
\[
 \phi_U
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^U)
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^U),
 \qquad
 V_U(P_0)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_X(x)\min\mathrm{QP}_x.
 \tag{18}
\]

Finally, an estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) is regular along every quadratic-mean differentiable submodel in either branch. Its regular influence component must therefore satisfy both branches' derivative covariance equations and belong to the common class in (14). Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}semiparametric\text{-}convolution\text{-}bound}\) to finite collections of branch submodels and taking their closed span gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_0}(\text{regular limit})
 \ge\inf_{\phi\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)}E_0[\phi^2]
 =E_0[\phi_U^2]=V_U(P_0).
 \tag{19}
\]
Equation (18) shows that this lower-bound envelope is sharp in the local tangent experiment. The cited branchwise laws in \(\mathrm{lem{:}sun\text{-}xie\text{-}zhang\text{-}branchwise\text{-}laws}\) concern distinct maintained-branch procedures and variances. Equations (18)--(19) add the sharp local benchmark imposed by regularity to either identifying branch; they do not construct an attaining estimator, replace either branch variance, or establish a standard error or multiplier procedure.

added_lemmas.statement:
At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) satisfying the displayed full-column-rank condition, the derivative of the profiled SC restriction in stratum \(x\) is
\[
 \dot r_{\mathrm{SC},x}
 =\{I_T-B(x)[B(x)^{\prime}B(x)]^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}\}
   \{\dot a(x)-\dot B(x)w(x)\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{rank}E_{P_{0,O}}[R_{\mathrm{SC},x}R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}]
 \le T-J.
\]
Equality holds when the covariance form of the residualized coordinates is positive definite on the \((T-J)\)-dimensional orthogonal complement of \(\operatorname{col}B(x)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(\Pi_x=B(x)\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}sc\text{-}rank}\) makes this the orthogonal projector onto the \(J\)-dimensional column space of \(B(x)\). Hence \(I_T-\Pi_x\) has rank \(T-J\). At an SC law, \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\). Differentiating \(\Pi_xB(x)=B(x)\) gives
\[
 \dot\Pi_xB(x)w(x)=(I_T-\Pi_x)\dot B(x)w(x).
 \tag{1}
\]
Since \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=(I_T-\Pi_x)a(x)\), equation (1) yields
\[
 \dot r_{\mathrm{SC},x}
 =(I_T-\Pi_x)\{\dot a(x)-\dot B(x)w(x)\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\), the same deterministic linear transformation relates the corresponding Riesz representers. Therefore the covariance range of \(R_{\mathrm{SC},x}\) is contained in \(\operatorname{range}(I_T-\Pi_x)\), proving the rank bound. If the residualized covariance form is positive definite on that range, its rank is the dimension of the range, namely \(T-J\).

added_lemmas.statement:
When \(J=T\), at every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\) satisfying the existing full-column-rank assumption, each \(B(x)\) is square and invertible, the profiled SC restriction is identically zero, and \(R_{\mathrm{SC},x}\) has rank zero for every \(x\in\mathcal X\). Therefore
\[
 \mathcal T_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)=\mathcal H_{P_0},
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\},
\]
and, at every such intersection law,
\[
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)
 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\},
 \qquad
 \phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}},
 \qquad
 V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\). When \(J=T\), the matrix \(B(x)\) is \(T\times T\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}sc\text{-}rank}\) gives
\[
 \lambda_{\min}\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}\ge\kappa_0>0,
 \tag{1}
\]
so \(B(x)\) is invertible. Consequently,
\[
 \{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}
 =B(x)^{-1}\{B(x)^{\prime}\}^{-1}
 \tag{2}
\]
and hence
\[
 B(x)\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}=I_T.
 \tag{3}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\), equation (3) makes \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=(I_T-I_T)a(x)=0\) throughout the full-rank neighborhood. Its derivative and Riesz representer are therefore zero. Equivalently, \(\mathrm{lem{:}sc\text{-}profiled\text{-}normal\text{-}rank}\) gives the upper bound \(T-J=0\), so the displayed SC normal Gram has rank zero.

The tangent normal form now gives
\[
 \mathcal T_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)
 =\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_{P_{0,O}}[0\cdot s]=0\}
 =\mathcal H_{P_0}
 \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)
 =\sum_xg_{\mathrm{SC},x}+\operatorname{span}\{0\}
 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\}.
 \tag{5}
\]
The union-envelope theorem proves that \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\) is nonempty. Since the second set in this intersection is the singleton in (5),
\[
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)
 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The definitions of the union canonical gradient and the two variance bounds then yield \(\phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\) and \(V_U=E_{P_{0,O}}[\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}^2]=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\).
added_lemmas.justification: This is the saturated-donor dual of the single-donor reduction: when \(J=T\), the SC restriction has no observed residual direction and the union envelope collapses to the SC oracle bound.
added_lemmas.gap: The existing branchwise results do not state this endpoint as a consequence of the PT--SC affine influence-class geometry.
added_lemmas.consumer: The reduction is a boundary check for implementations of the finite union-envelope quadratic program; it is not an attainment or inference theorem.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\), the common class \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\) is nonempty, and every estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) has convolution variance at least \(V_U(P_0)=E_{P_{0,O}}[\phi_U^2]\). If \((a_x^U,d_x^U)\) solves \(\mathrm{QP}_x\) built from the profiled \(J\)-coordinate PT normals and the SC normals, then
\[
 \phi_U=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\},
\]
and \(V_U\) is the sum of the stratum program values weighted by \(p_X(x)\). Relative to the branchwise laws in SunXieZhang2025, this supplies a sharp local lower-bound benchmark for procedures regular under PT-or-SC uncertainty at the stated intersection law. It neither replaces the branchwise asymptotic variances, furnishes an implemented standard error, nor proves attainment or multiplier validity.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing comparison sentence overclaims what a convolution lower bound delivers. The proved result adds a sharp local benchmark but neither replaces the branchwise variances nor constructs standard errors, attainment, or multiplier inference.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under the frozen definition of \(\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\), the requested uniform asymptotic-linear conclusion, and hence the requested four-part affirmative attainment result, is false in general. In particular, take \(P_0=P^{\star}\) and fixed margins that admit the witness with slack. For every sufficiently small nonzero \(\delta\), let \(Q_\delta\) retain the donor means and innovation laws of \(P^{\star}\) but replace the treated untreated mean path by \((-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta)\), and define
\[
 \Delta_\delta
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})
  -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star}).
\]
Then \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]\ge\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
\]
For every sample size, finite-coordinate splicing produces two elements of \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\) having the same observed law at that coordinate but different admissible chart labels. No single estimator can have both chart expansions uniformly. This obstruction proves no affirmative sequencewise continuation theorem; it merely does not rule out such a theorem after imposing a common local neighborhood, common bounds on the QMD scores and remainders, and exclusion of arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The previous final sentence could be read as an affirmative sequencewise continuation claim, but no such theorem remains in the retained graph. The narrowed statement records only the proved impossibility and the additional conditions under which that obstruction would cease to apply.

proposed.comparator_claim: The PT condition is the donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. The SC identification condition uses covariate-indexed weights shared across periods, summing to one with negative weights allowed and \(T\ge J\); its identification theorem does not itself require uniqueness. Its regular SC estimation theorem assumes a uniformly nonsingular reference-donor difference system, equivalent after reparameterization to full column rank of the augmented matrix \(B\).
Theorem 3.1 gives covariance-optimal PT weighting in the overidentified short-panel DiD model but no PT-or-SC union lower bound.
Section 3 constructs an intersection-efficient union-model estimator for a different finite-support odds-ratio problem, not the PT--SC ATT geometry studied here.
Proposition 1 derives the semiparametric efficiency bound for the two-group panel-DiD ATT.
Its cross-fit remainder theory is guidance for a repaired theorem with common rate control; it does not validate uniformity over a sequence class closed under finite-coordinate replacement.
Its analysis of drift under branchwise nuisance validity is guidance for a repaired theorem, but it does not remove the frozen class's finite-coordinate-splicing obstruction.
Its multiplier coupling theory is guidance for a repaired theorem after a genuinely uniform influence expansion is available; it supplies no such expansion for the frozen branch-switching class.

prose_updates.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification is valid on the union of conditional parallel trends and a full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction, but an analyst cannot choose the efficient influence law branch by branch when the valid restriction is unknown. Profiling the missing treated counterfactual change leaves a PT normal of rank at most \(J-1\), while profiling the full-rank SC mean restriction leaves an SC normal of rank at most \(T-J\). Their affine intersection yields a sharp local convolution lower bound computed by finite covariance-weighted programs, and observable Gram discrepancies characterize oracle adaptation. The equal-share three-group witness makes the efficiency cost strict; the single-donor and saturated-donor reductions recover the PT and SC oracle endpoints. The branch-chart extensions are definitions used to formulate a negative result: finite-coordinate splicing makes one uniformly chartwise asymptotic-linear expansion, and therefore the requested one-step, variance, and multiplier attainment theorem, false over the frozen local-sequence class.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the profiled PT and SC normal spans, solves their affine intersection by stratum covariance-weighted quadratic programs, characterizes simultaneous and one-sided oracle adaptation, supplies a strict three-group region, and proves the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoint reductions. The resulting envelope is a sharp local lower-bound benchmark for union-regular procedures, not an implemented standard error. The frozen branch-switching sequence class cannot support the requested uniform one-step and multiplier theorem because it is closed under arbitrary finite-coordinate splicing; no affirmative sequencewise continuation theorem remains in the retained graph.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-cell probabilities, conditional group-time means, restriction gradients, and covariance Grams are observable finite-dimensional nuisance objects for the lower-bound and oracle-adaptation calculations. The branch-chart extensions are definitions used to formulate the uniform-attainment obstruction. No cross-fitted projection estimator, variance estimator, data-driven chart coupling, or multiplier procedure is proved valid over the frozen local-sequence class.

prose_updates.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the identification anchor. Its PT condition is the donor-by-donor conditional final-change equality. Its SC hypothesis uses covariate-indexed weights common across every period, requires the weights to sum to one, permits negative weights, and assumes \(T\ge J\); the intercept row of \(B\) encodes the sum constraint. Its identification theorem does not itself require uniqueness. Its SC estimation theorem assumes a uniformly nonsingular reference-donor difference system \(M^{\prime}M\), which is equivalent after eliminating a reference donor to full column rank of the augmented matrix \(B\). The present model is a regular finite-support, uniform-overlap, uniform-moment, full-rank subclass of that identification model and matches its regular SC estimation class after reparameterization. SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, provide separate maintained-branch limit and multiplier laws; the present union envelope adds a sharp local lower-bound benchmark but does not replace those variances or furnish implemented inference. ChenSantAnnaXie2025 supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting, while the present PT geometry starts from all treated-versus-donor equalities and obtains donor-centering normals by profiling the latent treated change. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 studies a different finite-support union model. SantAnnaZhao2020 supplies the two-group panel-DiD gradient recovered by the single-donor reduction. NeweyRobins2018, ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016, and DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 are guidance only for a possible repaired theorem with genuinely uniform neighborhoods, common score and remainder bounds, and no finite-coordinate replacement. Lower-bound and impossibility conclusions transfer to estimators regular over the broader published PT-or-SC union by restriction to this subclass; sharpness is local only to the stated finite-support, uniform-margin, full-rank subclass. RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska analysis in SunXieZhang2025 motivate the lower-bound diagnostic but receive no new standard-error procedure from this paper.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The union envelope is a local regularity lower bound at fixed-rank intersection laws. It is not an attaining estimator, a usable standard error, or a multiplier-confidence procedure. The negative theorem applies to the frozen sequence class because arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements defeat uniformity; it does not settle a redesigned sequence class with one common neighborhood and common QMD and remainder bounds. Rank failure, vanishing overlap, changing covariate support, covariance degeneracy, and weight-boundary restrictions require different local experiments.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved deliverables are the intersection tangent-normal characterization, the finite covariance-weighted union convolution lower bound, the oracle-adaptation Gram tests, the strict three-group witness, and the single-donor and saturated-donor endpoint reductions. The bound is sharp in the stated local tangent experiment and transfers as a lower bound to procedures regular over the broader published union by restriction, but sharpness is claimed only for the regular finite-support, uniform-margin, full-rank subclass. The frozen local-sequence class makes a single uniformly chartwise asymptotic-linear expansion, and hence the requested one-step, variance-consistency, and multiplier-coverage theorem, false by finite-coordinate splicing. The branch-chart extensions are definitions used in that obstruction. No positive sequencewise continuation theorem remains; the obstruction merely does not rule one out under additional uniform-neighborhood and common-remainder assumptions.
